---
title: "Advanced Command Line documentation"
description: "Command-line reference for the jackmoebius CLI: expose apps, manage routing and channel reservations, and script JackMoebius from the terminal."
---

`jackmoebius` is the command-line control tool. It talks to the `jackmoebiusd` daemon
over a local socket. Most commands require the daemon (hence a running JACK server);
`version` works even when everything is stopped.

Apps are matched by their **display name** (`Safari`, `Music`) or their **bundle ID**
(`com.apple.Safari`), case-insensitive.

```bash
jackmoebius <command> [arguments]
```

## Version & lifecycle

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `jackmoebius version` | Print the version + copyright (works while stopped). Aliases: `--version`, `-v`. |
| `jackmoebius start` | Launch `jackmoebiusd` (JACK must be up). |
| `jackmoebius stop` | Stop the daemon cleanly. |
| `jackmoebius status` | Daemon, device, JACK and transport health, shared input, capacity (`--verbose` for details). |
| `jackmoebius doctor [--json]` | Say what is wrong and what to do about it. See [Doctor](#doctor). |

```bash
$ jackmoebius version
JackMoebius 1.1.0
Copyright © 2026 Éric Bavu. All rights reserved.
```

## License & trial

JackMoebius runs as a **14-day trial**, then needs a license. These commands work **while
the daemon is stopped** (like `version`); reading the status needs no network.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `jackmoebius license` | Show the trial / license status. Add `--json` for a machine-readable form. |
| `jackmoebius license activate <KEY>` | Activate this Mac with your license key (**needs an internet connection**). |
| `jackmoebius license refresh` | Re-validate the license online now (e.g. after freeing a slot on another Mac). |

```bash
$ jackmoebius license
Trial — 9 day(s) left

$ jackmoebius license activate XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX
License activated on this Mac (1/5 machines used).
```

A license is **perpetual** and, once activated, stays valid **offline indefinitely**, so you're
never locked out for lack of network. A license covers up to its activation limit of Macs
(shown in the status); to move it to another Mac, contact support.

## Apps & routing

Every app has two directions, and for each one you choose where it goes. That choice is a **spec**:

| Spec | What it means |
|---|---|
| `shared` | The common **JackMoebius** device, with nothing to set in the app. **Output:** a stereo pair of its own, separate from every other app. **Input:** the same two channels (`shared_input_1/2` in JACK) for every app in this mode. |
| `private` | A device of its own, **JackMoebius for <App>**, that you select in the app. 2 channels. |
| `private=N` or `N` | The same with N channels, from 1 to 64 (mono included). A bare number always means a card of N channels. |

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `jackmoebius apps` | List CoreAudio apps seen by the driver (per-app state: exposed, backing, channels, capture-capable, blacklisted). |
| `jackmoebius add <App> [--in [<spec>]] [--out [<spec>]]` | Expose an app's input and/or output; its JACK box appears. |
| `jackmoebius remove <App> [--in] [--out]` | Hide an app's box (the channel reservation is kept). |
| `jackmoebius list` | Currently exposed boxes, with per-box **routing status**. |

A flag without a spec asks you the question (at a terminal). `add`, `remove` and `clear` with neither `--in` nor
`--out` ask which side you mean. In a script nothing is guessed: say it on the command line.

```bash
$ jackmoebius add Music --out shared
exposed 'Music' on channels 2/3 (the app plays to the JackMoebius default output)

$ jackmoebius add Safari --in shared
'Safari' reads the shared input (ports shared_input_1/2, the same two channels for every app in this mode) ...

# one device, JackMoebius for REAPER, with 8 inputs and 16 outputs
$ jackmoebius add REAPER --in private=8 --out private=16

$ jackmoebius add "QuickTime Player"
Which side of 'QuickTime Player' do you want to expose?
  1) output   the app's sound towards JACK
  2) input    JACK towards the app
  3) both
Choice [1/2/3, q to cancel]:
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Shared or a card of its own?"}
- Use **shared** for apps that have no device menu (browsers, dictation, many small apps): they follow the Mac's
  default input and output, which JackMoebius takes care of.
- Use a **card** when the app lets you choose its input or output device in its settings and you want channels of
  its own (a DAW, a video call, a recorder). Then select **JackMoebius for <App>** in the app.
- If an app has a single device setting for input **and** output and you want it on a card, make **both** directions private
  (`--in private --out private`): a card that only has an input has no output for it. Such an app can also stay on the shared
  device: leave both directions shared and select **JackMoebius** in it.
:::

### Changing a direction

A card only holds the directions you made private. When you change one direction of an app:

- Adding a private direction to an app that already has a card for the other one, or changing the number of
  channels, **rebuilds** the card: the app sees its device go and come back for a moment.
- Moving a direction back to `shared` while the other direction keeps a card **leaves the card as it is**. That
  direction is no longer wired, so choose the shared **JackMoebius** device for it in the app. Its channels stay
  reserved until the card is deleted or rebuilt.
- Moving it back when nothing else needs the card **deletes** the card. An app that had selected it falls back to
  another device.

The routing status in `list` is `ok` / `mismatch` / `idle` / `absent`. It reports whether the
app actually uses the right JackMoebius device (see the [IPC protocol](ipc.qmd#routing-status)).

## Reservations

Channel reservations are **persistent**: an app keeps its channels across restarts, so
a saved patchbay restores itself. `remove` hides a box but keeps the reservation;
`clear` frees it.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `jackmoebius assignments` | Show the persistent channel reservations (outputs, then private inputs). |
| `jackmoebius clear <App> [--in] [--out]` | Drop an app's reservation (frees its channels; the card goes when nothing else needs it). Works with the daemon stopped, too. |

## Volume

Per-app **output volume**, with a "cadenas" (lock): locked = follows the volume of the
*JackMoebius* device; unlocked = its own independent gain.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `jackmoebius volume <App>` | Show the app's `{locked, gain}`. |
| `jackmoebius volume <App> lock` \| `unlock` | Lock to master, or take independent control. |
| `jackmoebius volume <App> <gain>` | Set an independent linear gain (`1.0` = unity, `0.0` = mute). |

## Doctor

`jackmoebius doctor` lists what is wrong and what to do about it: the daemon or JACK not running, the background
service missing or switched off, an app that does not use its card, a bus that is nearly full, another account
using JackMoebius. Add `--json` for the structured list (stable codes, which JackMate shows as banners). The exit
status is 1 when there is an error. It also works with the daemon stopped, with what it can check on its own.

## Blacklist

Apps you never want proposed for routing (hidden from `add` and from the selector).
Ships with Audio MIDI Setup, [JackMate](https://jackmate.app), and Zoom
(see the note below); fully revertable.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `jackmoebius blacklist --show` | List the blacklist. |
| `jackmoebius blacklist --add <App>` | Blacklist an app (refused if it's currently exposed). |
| `jackmoebius blacklist --remove <App>` | Un-blacklist. |
| `jackmoebius blacklist --reset` | Restore the shipped defaults. |

::: {.callout-warning title="Zoom is not supported"}
**Zoom is blacklisted by default and does not work with JackMoebius.** On macOS, Zoom
rejects virtual audio devices, even when wrapped in an Aggregate Device, unlike most
apps. This is a Zoom limitation (its handling of virtual devices is undocumented), not
a JackMoebius bug: every other app we tested (Microsoft Teams, Audacity, OBS,
browsers…) works normally.
:::

## Shell completion

The installer ships **zsh** and **bash** completions (commands, `--in` and `--out` with their values, and live
app names for `add` / `remove` / `clear` / `blacklist`).

The zsh completion file is installed on the completion path
(`/usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions`), but zsh only activates completions once your
shell has initialized its completion system. If `jackmoebius `<kbd>Tab</kbd> does nothing
(typically on a fresh account with no `~/.zshrc`), add this line to your `~/.zshrc` and
open a new terminal:

```zsh
autoload -Uz compinit && compinit
```

Most setups (Oh My Zsh, a customized `~/.zshrc`, …) already do this. It's the standard
step for **every** tool's zsh completion. The installer deliberately does not edit your
shell configuration.

For **bash** (a minority on macOS, whose default shell is zsh), the completion is
installed in the standard Homebrew directory `/usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d`. It
activates automatically once you have `bash-completion` installed and sourced
(`brew install bash-completion`, then source it from your `~/.bash_profile`). Again, a
shell-config step the installer leaves to you.
